findings.failure_scenario: MySQL InnoDB defaults to REPEATABLE READ. UpdateLog::snapshot and UpdateLog::append run in a transaction whose first statement is NodeReadRepository::find (DatabaseCollaborativeState::lock line 53), a plain SELECT that fixes the snapshot. An append that commits after that read is visible to lockHead (SELECT … FOR UPDATE, so head_seq becomes 1) and invisible to the plain collaboration_updates read at line 113 and the plain Document read of yjs_state at line 107. POST /v1/collaboration/hub/load with X-Vaulter-Collab-Protocol: 2 then returns 200 with head_seq 1 and tail []. The hub treats the room as caught up and never replays the committed update. The same snapshot makes receipt() at line 143 miss a receipt committed by an overlapping append of the same update_id and payload; the second insert hits the updates unique key or the receipts primary key and the request fails with a database error instead of the original seq. PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED and SQLite do not split these reads, so the sqlite tests stay green.
findings.reproduction: Not executed (read-only). Static trace of UpdateLog::snapshot and receipt() against InnoDB consistent reads versus locking reads; the same split is already documented on NodeReadRepository::siblingQuery.

triage_reproduction.observed: lock() opens the transaction with a plain SELECT (nodes->find). UpdateLog::snapshot reads Document (line 107), collaboration_updates (113) and receipt() (143) with plain selects, while lockHead uses FOR UPDATE. Under InnoDB REPEATABLE READ the plain reads use the snapshot taken at the first read. The repo already documents the same split at NodeReadRepository:504. A MySQL run is forbidden by D41, so the failure itself was not executed; only the code path was confirmed.

findings.failure_scenario: loadLog reads content from $room->document, which open() loaded before UpdateLog::snapshot locks the document. A REST PUT, allowed while the pending marker is null, commits content B and state_version 4 after open() has read content A and version 3. The locked snapshot then reports state_version 4 and checkpoint null, while content is still A. HubLoadedV2 requires content and describes it as the seed before the first checkpoint, so the hub seeds A and a later checkpoint overwrites B. This window exists on every engine.
findings.reproduction: Not executed. open() at CollaborationHub.php:86 loads the aggregate; loadLog line 221 reads that instance after snapshot() returns.

triage_reproduction.observed: loadLog (lines 211, 222) reads content/type/schema_version from $room->document, which open() loaded at line 86 before UpdateLog::snapshot takes the locks. state_version comes from the locked snapshot. So the seed content and the state_version can come from different moments.

findings.failure_scenario: A subject holds a room JWT for epoch 1 and no longer has View. The document still exists in that tenant with collab_epoch 2. open() throws CollaborationEpochMismatchException (409, context expected 1, actual 2) before ability() runs, on both append and load v2. The same call after the node is deleted is 404 node_not_found. A hidden document whose generation moved is therefore distinguishable from a missing one. Another tenant is rejected earlier and stays 404.
findings.reproduction: Not executed. Epoch comparison is CollaborationHub.php:87-88; assertVisible runs only after open() returns (append line 189, loadLog line 209).

triage_reproduction.observed: open() throws CollaborationEpochMismatchException at lines 87-88 before ability() at line 96. assertVisible runs only in append/loadLog after open() returns (lines 189, 209). A subject without View therefore gets 409 for an existing document with a moved epoch and 404 for a missing one.

findings.failure_scenario: POST /v1/collaboration/hub/append with no Content-Length, or a Content-Length that is not all digits, and a body larger than limits.request_bytes, and without a hub signature. LimitHubAppend calls $request->getContent(), allocates the whole body, then throws 413 collaboration_update_too_large. ResolveCollaborationCall runs only after that middleware. The adopted rule is to refuse an over-limit body from Content-Length before the body is read into memory. A numeric Content-Length above the limit is rejected on line 28-30 without that read.
